exact_source_excerpts: A finite multiset on $X$ is a function $m:X\to\mathbb N_0$ with finite support
Two finite multisets are equal exactly when their multiplicity functions agree at every element of $X$.
before_evidence: Conversely, if all multiplicities agree at every x in X, the two multiplicity functions are equal as functions and hence are the same finite multiset. The finite-support requirement remains in force for both inputs.
after_evidence: Definition, the following declared clauses/formulas: `A finite multiset on $X$ is a function $m:X\to\mathbb N_0$ with finite support`; `Two finite multisets are equal exactly when their multiplicity functions agree at every element of $X$.`. Conversely, if all multiplicities agree at every x in X, the two multiplicity functions are equal as functions and hence are the same finite multiset. The finite-support requirement remains in force for both inputs.
